name: Singapore Math
line: Singapore Math is printed books an adult places and grades. AMP places, checks and reviews at every answer.
description: AMP vs Singapore Math: a respected print method beside a program that checks every answer, finds gaps strand by strand and schedules review.
verdict: Singapore Math's books teach a respected method, from objects to pictures to symbols, and its free placement tests give a family a clear way in [1][3]. But a book cannot check an answer, find a gap in one part of math, or bring an old skill back on a schedule; the adult does all three. AMP does them at every problem, from counting through precalculus, and still prints paper.

reasons.title: Every answer is checked and explained
reasons.body: Singapore Math is a set of printed textbooks and workbooks [1]. A page cannot tell a child that an answer is wrong, or why; an adult has to. AMP marks every answer, shows the correct one and the worked steps, and only then moves on. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.05 for marking right or wrong alone [9].

reasons.title: A level in each strand, not one book
reasons.body: Singapore Math places a child by half-year book. Its placement tests take at least an hour each, are not meant to be scored, and do not cover every topic in a level [3]. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems, with no separate test, and keeps a separate level in each of 14 strands of math that every answer adjusts. A learner can be at grade 6 in geometry and grade 3 in fractions, and practice targets each.

reasons.title: AMP finds and repairs gaps on its own
reasons.body: Singapore Math's placement tests judge a level as a whole, and the company tells parents to check the scope and sequence for topics the tests leave out [3]. We found no automatic route back to a missing prerequisite in its materials [1][3]. In AMP, two misses in a row on a skill send practice to what that skill builds on. An answer given after a hint is recorded but does not count toward mastery.

reasons.title: Old skills come back on a schedule
reasons.body: We found no review schedule in Singapore Math's published materials [1][3]. AMP brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, then 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and 1 month, mixed with other topics, and a miss restarts the schedule. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on a test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [8].

reasons.title: One program from counting to precalculus
reasons.body: Dimensions Math, listed as the company's most popular curriculum, runs from pre-kindergarten to grade 8, and its placement tests stop at the end of grade 5; Primary Mathematics tests reach grade 6 [1][3]. AMP runs from counting through Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 and Precalculus on one map of 336 skills. A learner moves into the next band when ready, with no new books to order.

reasons.title: Workbooks made for one learner, with worked keys
reasons.body: Singapore Math's books are printed editions, not made for one child, and orders ship in 5 to 14 business days [2]. AMP prints a new workbook whenever one is needed, built from the learner's own answers, with practice, skills due for review and a challenge section. Each comes with a worked answer key, and results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

rows.buyers: Families and schools. Printed books by grade, each in A and B half-year books, with free shipping over $100 in the contiguous U.S. [2][3].
rows.range: Dimensions Math: pre-kindergarten to grade 8. Primary Mathematics in several editions, with placement tests from 1A to 6B [1][3].
rows.start: Free placement tests, untimed and not scored. The adult reads the child's work and picks a half-year book [3].
rows.teaching: Printed lessons that move from concrete objects to pictures to symbols [1]. Dimensions Math also offers a video subscription [1].
rows.next: The books' order, a half-year book at a time. Placement works the same way: pass 2A, take 2B [3].
rows.mastery: No numeric rule found. Placement tests judge a level by the adult's reading of the work, not a score [3].
rows.review: No review schedule found in its published materials [1][3].
rows.print: Printed textbooks and workbooks, shipped in 5 to 14 business days; not made for one child [2].
rows.adult: Reads an unscored placement test to choose the level, orders each book, and checks the child's work [2][3].
rows.reports: No gradebook or progress reports found for the books [1].
rows.evidence: Singapore Math: no Evidence for ESSA rating, and no studies met WWC standards (2015) [6][7]. HMH's Math in Focus, a separate program, is rated Strong [4].

theirs: Singapore Math Inc. sells the Singapore approach to math to U.S. families and schools, and says it was the first to bring it to the U.S. [1]. Its main series are Dimensions Math, for pre-kindergarten to grade 8 and listed as its most popular curriculum, and Primary Mathematics, sold in several editions [1]. The company owns the Singapore Math trademark jointly with Marshall Cavendish Education [1].

The books teach with concrete objects first, then pictures, then symbols, in what the company calls a "mastery spiral" [1]. Each grade comes in two books: A for the first half of the year, B for the second [3]. A family starts with a free placement test, untimed and not scored; the adult watches how the child works and which mistakes come up, then picks the book [3]. Supplements add extra practice, fluency work and word problems [1].

Math in Focus is a different program: a school edition of the Singapore approach for kindergarten to grade 8, published by Houghton Mifflin Harcourt with digital tools on its own platform [5]. This page compares AMP with Singapore Math Inc.'s books and names Math in Focus only where its evidence comes up.
credit: A clear, well-known teaching method: concrete objects, then pictures, then symbols [1][5]. AMP teaches with written lessons, worked examples and films, not a sequence that starts with objects in the hand.
Math on paper, with no screen and no connection. AMP prints workbooks, but its practice needs a browser and an internet connection.
Free placement tests for every half-year level, and a plain path for homeschool families [2][3].
Real evidence for the approach in schools: HMH's Math in Focus, a separate Singapore-style program, is rated Strong by Evidence for ESSA [4]. AMP has no outcome study yet.

theirs: We found no outcome study of Dimensions Math or Primary Mathematics on Singapore Math Inc.'s site, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse, as of November 2026. The home page cites no studies [1]. Evidence for ESSA lists Singapore Math without a rating, saying no studies met its inclusion requirements; the page does not mention Primary Mathematics or Dimensions Math [6]. The What Works Clearinghouse found no studies of Singapore Mathematics (reviewed as Primary Mathematics) that met its standards, in a report dated December 2015 [7].

The Singapore-style program with real evidence is HMH's Math in Focus. Evidence for ESSA rates it Strong: four studies, 3,444 students in grades 2 to 5, an average effect size of +0.15 on standardized measures [4]. One study, by Jaciw and colleagues at Empirical Education, is titled as a randomized trial; the others are by the Educational Research Institute of America, listed as HMH reports, and JEM & R LLC [4]. Teachers in the studies had summer training and four whole days of training during the year [4]. That is a school program taught by trained teachers, and its rating does not carry over to books a parent buys from Singapore Math Inc.
ours: Two well-studied methods are ones a printed book leaves to the adult. Mixed, spaced practice scored 62% against 38% a month later in a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, though on the researchers' own test, and the mixed practice was also spaced [8]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in many ages and subjects, feedback that explains averaged 0.49, and marking right or wrong alone averaged 0.05 [9]. AMP builds both into every problem, with no planning by the adult. We expect that to show in outcomes, and we have committed in public to measuring it.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: You love teaching math yourself and want a book with a clear method of objects, pictures and symbols.
You want math on paper, with no screen and no connection.
You want free placement tests and printed books for each half of the year.
You run a school that wants a teacher-led Singapore-style curriculum with an Evidence for ESSA rating. That is HMH's Math in Focus [4].
amp: You want every answer checked and explained, without grading it yourself.
Your child is further along in one part of math than another.
You want old skills to come back on a schedule, without planning it.
Your learner is heading past grade 8, toward algebra and precalculus.
You like your Singapore books and want daily practice and review beside them.

questions.question: Is Singapore Math the same as Math in Focus?
questions.answer: No. Math in Focus is HMH's school program based on the Singapore approach [5]. Singapore Math Inc. sells Dimensions Math and Primary Mathematics [1]. Math in Focus's Strong rating from Evidence for ESSA does not apply to them; Evidence for ESSA lists Singapore Math without a rating [4][6].

questions.question: Can I use AMP with Singapore Math?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems and keeps a level in each strand, checks every answer and brings old skills back on a schedule. A parent can also pick a skill on AMP's map to practice the topic the book is on.

questions.question: Is AMP more expensive than Singapore Math?
questions.answer: AMP costs $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child, and $399 or $39 for each more, with a full refund within 30 days. Singapore Math sells printed books by grade level, in A and B half-year books, with free shipping on orders over $100 in the contiguous U.S. [2][3]; its store lists current prices. AMP's price covers every level from counting through precalculus, unlimited personalized workbooks, and the checking and review scheduling.
